record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Are Kakutani equivalence classes Borel sets, and if they are, what is the complexity of the isomorphism relation restricted to a Kakutani equivalence class?

evidence.quote: Question 2.7 (Rodriguez Hertz). Are Kakutani equivalence classes Borel? If so what is the complexity of the isomorphism relation on that class?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, endowed with the weak topology. Two transformations $T,S\in\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if there exist measurable sets $A,B\subseteq X$ of positive measure such that the induced transformation $T_A$ on $A$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to the induced transformation $S_B$ on $B$ (where $T_A(x)$ is defined as $T^{n(x)}(x)$ with $n(x)$ the first return time of $x$ to $A$, and analogously for $S_B$). This defines an equivalence relation $\mathcal{K}$ on $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ whose equivalence classes are called Kakutani equivalence classes.

(a) For which (if any) Kakutani equivalence classes $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}\subseteq\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ is $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$?

(b) Whenever such a class is Borel, determine the descriptive set-theoretic complexity of the measure-theoretic isomorphism equivalence relation $\cong$ (where $T\cong S$ iff there exists $\varphi\in\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ with $\varphi T=S\varphi$) restricted to $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}$, in the sense of Borel reducibility among Borel/analytic equivalence relations.
artifact.category_tag: descriptive set theory of ergodic transformations
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Foreman–Gerber–Kunde and Foreman–Weiss) has shown that the Kakutani equivalence relation and the isomorphism relation on ergodic/weakly mixing measure-preserving transformations are not Borel (anti-classification results), but the specific question of which individual Kakutani equivalence classes are Borel and the Borel/analytic complexity of isomorphism restricted to such a class does not appear to have a complete answer in the literature, and is generally treated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for the Kakutani equivalence relation
status_evidence.snippet: The Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of a standard non-atomic probability space is not a Borel set.
status_evidence.claim: The full Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic MPTs is not Borel, but the question of individual classes being Borel and the complexity of isomorphism on them remains open.

status_evidence.title: Descriptive Kakutani equivalence
status_evidence.snippet: Descriptive Kakutani equivalence of Borel functions; classification results in the Borel setting.
status_evidence.claim: Descriptive Kakutani equivalence is studied but the measure-theoretic version raised by Rodriguez Hertz remains a stated open question.
